title: Review of c18's flshell2 (IBMED): on fresh seeds 8 and 9 the shelled gliders divide (generation 7/4), travel 10.7-14 body lengths, and a food-cut daughter dies (seed 9 by ~300 t, seed 8 by ~450-470 t) while its fed twin persists; the shell forms (peak S 0.38 at 9 px, closed 62%) but often wraps 2-4 bodies and speeds them only modestly
summary: Re-ran world.py unchanged on fresh seeds 8 and 9 (labkit, 128^2, t=800), the h5=0 ablation on the same seeds, c18's shellprof.py and speedcmp.py, and dfork.py (seed 9 for 300 t; seed 8 for 300 and 600 t). Packs: 10 and 4 persistent splits, generation 7 and 4, merge/split 0.84 and 0.82; 41 tracks move >= 1 body length on each, max 10.7 and 14.0. Shell around isolated bodies: S peak ~0.38 at r~9 px, inside <0.12, median closure 24/24 sectors, 62% fully closed (shellprof.png). Feedback ablation h5=0: median top-track speed 0.40 -> 0.52 (seed 8) and 0.49 -> 0.51 (seed 9), moving tracks 26 -> 41 and 30 -> 41, max body lengths 12.4 -> 10.7 and 7.6 -> 14.0. Forks: seed 9 (t=190, 18 px): the starved daughter shrinks to ~3 by t~490 while the fed-twin daughter grows; seed 8 (t=155, 18.5 px): after 300 t the starved daughter has only halved (61 -> 32), and with 600 t it reaches ~0 by t~600-625, after which the following disk hops onto a passing body (dl8.png); the fed-twin daughter persists.

observations.M: speedcmp.json: 41 moving tracks per seed, max 10.7 and 14.0 body lengths
observations.E: forks/df9.png (starved daughter gone by t~490, fed twin persists) and forks/dl8.png (gone by t~600-625 in the 600 t fork)
observations.D: rerun/pack/seed8/lineage.png: 10 persistent splits, generation 7; seed 9: 4, generation 4

seeds_run.result: pass (E only in the 600 t fork; the 300 t fork shows halving, not death)

controls_run.E: forks/ (dfork.py fed twin vs food cut following one daughter, seeds 8 and 9)

by_construction: E (matter is built only from food)
verdicts.limitation: B not endorsed: the S ring is a set-point readout at ~9 px with an empty gap between body and shell, and in the crowded phase (t > ~350) one shell often wraps 2-4 bodies (rerun/pack/seed8/sheet.png), so it does not consistently belong to one individual; its work (speed) is small and mixed on my seeds (+3-30% median speed, max body lengths down on seed 8). Death after the cut takes 300-470 t, longer than in the h5=0 world. Genealogy is reticulate (merge/split 0.82-0.84). Planted patch (no S).
